clusters.synthesis: These candidates all describe securing agentic systems: tool side effects, code-security analysis, development-time security, broad autonomous-system risk, and supply-chain abuse.
These candidates converge on the same operating model: engineers embedded with customers, adapting the product from real usage, often with platform constraints and human-in-the-loop workflow splits.
This frames software factories as an end-to-end system for turning requests into shipped software through planning, implementation, review, and production.
This is about choosing the right environment or host for each agent task.
This focuses on coordinating pod-level and node-level scaling instead of relying on a single autoscaling layer.
This centers on the runtime path from agent through MCP client and server to the target resource, where authorization can be enforced.
These candidates describe independent verification or human outer-loop control supervising agent execution rather than letting the same loop self-grade.
This is about safely patching vulnerable dependencies across many repositories while keeping pull requests reviewable.
This describes grounding agent behavior in organizational and public knowledge sources.
This proposes harnesses that start work, listen for external events, and adapt over time.
This treats open-weight models as a practical production alternative.
This is about reward schemes that compare grouped samples to balance correctness and efficiency.
This uses community detection to surface clusters and hidden themes across a corpus.
This is about sandbox placement and orchestration that account for snapshot lineage and node state.
This describes repeated agent runs over tasks to collect trajectories and scores.
This assigns the right proof method to each change or task.
This captures intent by marking elements directly on screen instead of writing a long instruction.
This inspects agent traces to understand why a failure occurred.
This treats ephemeral sandboxes as isolated workspaces for code, browsing, and file work, not as the durable source of truth.
This packages project metadata so agents can read, summarize, and act on a changing system.
This is about a collaborative work environment where humans and agents reason together.
This evaluates outputs as full distributions rather than only as point estimates.
This uses data from real workflows, reasoning traces, and decision sequences rather than only final outputs.
This warns against collapsing the visual diversity of a marketplace during edits.
This emphasizes explicit repository constraints and proof before agents write code.
This distinguishes operator assumptions from the real constraints in the environment.
This evaluates models in a live hidden system with limited information and no source access.
This says evaluation design determines what an autonomous research system optimizes for.
This is a pre-answer memory layer that gives agents company definitions, documentation, and failure history.
This applies different trust rules when facts have multiple parents and mixed-source ancestry.
This keeps transaction, account, device, and payment domains isolated while integrating agents into event-sourced systems.
This links domain concepts to underlying systems of record through a semantic layer.
This compares expert-defined schemas with data-driven ontology extension.
This frames video understanding as reusable infrastructure built from memory and harnesses.
This argues agents can work from HTML/web substrates rather than richer media pipelines.
This argues an organization’s durable AI advantage comes from internal processes and tacit knowledge captured in its data model.
These candidates make the same claim: local AI became broadly useful once models and harnesses improved together.
This uses broad models, consensus labeling, and curation to produce narrower specialized models or datasets.
This treats the engineer’s harness-improvement speed as the main production bottleneck.
This argues graph-based memory is more useful than more tokens for connected retrieval.
This emphasizes models coordinating and verifying multi-step work.
This defines AI systems by business results rather than generic answer quality.
This tracks the sequence of steps that produced a financial metric or ratio.
This constrains edits, approvals, and self-modification through policy.
This covers the operational burden on security leaders facing oversight expectations for agent decisions.
This is feedback from users and products that shapes the next round of training or behavior.
This packages observability context as composable skills for agent workflows.
These candidates both describe durable preference instructions and the need to remove empty no-op guidance.
The practice of tuning an AI agent's instructions, tone, and action boundaries for a specific enterprise.
Keeping GPU workers busy by allocating sandboxes from a demand-sized warm pool.
Whether content stays consistent across frames and shots over time.
